page.layout: One page of running text in one column; a marginal note in the left margin, beside the middle of the text.

main_text.p: Huic sententiæ patrocinatur Galenus lib. 1. de sanit.tuen. ubi de lacte nutricis ait, debere id esse bene temperatum, quale certe erit, si sanguis eius, quam optimus sit. Isautem talis est, qui nec flava, nec atra bile, nec serosa aut aquosa abundat substantia. Et paulo post ibidem: Optimum lac est, quod gustanti olfacienti, plane suave aspicienti seu intuenti candidum, et æquale, liquidiq, & crassi medium apparebit, quod vitiosum est, aut crassum, aut caseosum, aut liquidum, aut serosum ac lividum, tum consistentia colore, ipso inæquale videbitur, gu-stantibusq, amarorem, aut salsedinem, aut qua-litatem saltem exhibebit extraneam. Idem l. 7. de morb. curandis bonum lac appellat, quod nullam externam qualitatem odore, vel gustu præ se fert, sed quam dulcissimum est, si-bique ipsi continuum, et prout lacti convenit, splendens, & super omnia, similes habet partes. Hæc Galenus. Caeterum cum probatissimum lac infigni vi nutriendi polleat, perbelleq; alat, usu tamen eius non omnibus æque sit salubris, videndum ulterius, Lac qui-bus pro-fit, vel obsit.quibus sumpsisse ex usu sit, quibus non. Certum est, si bene concoquatur, nutrire, probosq; humores generare, & dum concoquitur illa attollit & inflat, petitq; caput etiam in sanis, teste Gal. in expositione apho-rism. 64. l. 5. page.notes: The left marginal note is printed in smaller type and is transcribed in full where it stands. The catchword "alis" at the lower right is read from the scan and may be the start of the next page. The word "bique" (si-bique) is uncertain: the scan shows "biq," and I read it as "bique" [?]. The printed "sumpfifse" is read as "sumpsisse"; the long s is written as plain s throughout. The line ending "etiam in sanis" has a faint final letter, and "aphorism." is read as "apho-rism." from the printed hyphen. The printed "vbi" and "vfus" are written with u as vowels.
